target_customer: Oncologists, hospitals and pharma running clinical trials who need data-driven treatment monitoring and biomarker tools
problem: Oncologists struggle to know whether a cancer treatment is working and which drug to use when; CCG used blood draws and machine learning to track response.
business_model: B2B software and diagnostic services to clinical and research customers
product_category: Precision oncology software and ctDNA monitoring

founders.name: John Cassidy
founders.background_notes: Called Dr John W Cassidy, CEO and cofounder, in the Dante Labs acquisition release (2021-06-23).

founders.name: Nirmesh Patel
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a scientist turned founder.

founders.name: Evaline Tsai
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without background.

exit.reason: Dante Labs planned to combine CCG's OncOS machine learning oncology software with its Immensa genomics interpretation software; terms not disclosed.

competitors.name: Inivata
competitors.what: Cambridge-based liquid biopsy company developing ctDNA blood tests for cancer treatment
competitors.funding_then: Raised a 31.5 million pound Series A in January 2016 after a 4 million pound seed

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining ctDNA sequencing data, clinical data and machine learning to predict treatment response needed genomics and clinical validation, which is hard for a seed-stage team.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical and genomic datasets and validated biomarkers could compound, but they depended on hospital partnerships and larger rivals had far more capital.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dante Labs, a genomics company, acquired CCG in June 2021; no incumbent copying was found.

market_need_then: Precision oncology and liquid biopsy attracted heavy investment by 2016 (Inivata's 31.5 million pound Series A), showing demand for treatment-monitoring tools.

branding.domain_note: ccg.ai was used from at least 2020; it now redirects to an Atom.com name-for-sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission stated as each patient getting the right drug at the right time to beat their cancer

branding.brand_signature: OncOS, the precision oncology software platform

brand_strength.rationale: Used the descriptive name Cambridge Cancer Genomics and the short form CCG.ai side by side; press mainly covered the acquisition and no community signals were found.

outcome_analysis: Cambridge Cancer Genomics raised an early seed, took part in YC in Summer 2017, and was acquired by Dante Labs in June 2021 with undisclosed terms, so the YC Inactive label reflects the acquisition and not a clear failure. Press does not say whether the sale was a strong exit or a soft landing, and the amount raised (7.2 million pounds per Cambridge Judge Business School) exceeds the rounds recorded, so the history is incomplete.
notes: YC status is Inactive while the exit is an acquisition; the YC label reflects the 2021 sale. Seedtable gives a $4.5M seed dated 2018-12-31 while CB Insights dates a seed to 2017-08-22 and reports a total of $4.67M over 6 rounds; the two entries may be the same round and each rests on a single database. The 2020-02 incubator round comes from CB Insights snippets only. The Cambridge Judge Business School page says 7.2 million pounds raised in total, more than the recorded amounts, so earlier rounds may be missing. CB Insights financials returned 403 on direct fetch, so its figures come from search snippets. Founders other than John Cassidy appear only on the YC page. Founded 2015 per YC and 2016 per JBS. Inivata is a liquid biopsy competitor whose source predates the batch; CCG's product was software on top of ctDNA data, so the overlap is partial. The ccg.ai fetch redirected to a for-sale page. Audit fix: the placeholder date 2018-12-31 on the Seedtable 4.5M seed is replaced with 2018-12 (month only; Seedtable shows a day-level stamp that looks like a default). The 2017-08-22 CB Insights round may be the YC investment (unconfirmed). CB Insights reports 6 rounds totalling 4.67M, of which only three are itemised here.
